svg.title: Culturing microorganisms
svg.desc: Binary fission: One bacterial cell → two. With nutrients and suitable temperature, division may take 20 minutes; use the given time. 1 → 2 → 4 → 8: repeated doubling, not addition. No nucleus; bacteria do not use mitosis. Growing a culture: Broth: nutrients for growth. Agar: surface for colonies (a visible group from an initial cell/group). Uncontaminated cultures allow fair antimicrobial comparisons. Aseptic technique keeps unwanted microorganisms out. Sterile equipment: Sterilise dishes/medium to remove unwanted microbes. Flame the loop; cool it so it does not kill the culture. Open lid briefly to limit airborne contamination. Follow school handling/disposal procedures. Safe incubation: Tape edges, not a full seal: prevents opening; allows gas exchange. Invert: condensation cannot drip onto culture. Maximum 25°C in school limits harmful human pathogens. Do not open incubated plates. Antimicrobial discs: Use asepsis to prepare a lawn on sterile agar. Add antibiotic/antiseptic discs and a solvent-only control. Incubate safely; measure inhibition zones. Repeat and calculate a mean for each substance. Variables & conclusions: Change: substance/type or concentration. Measure: zone diameter or area. Keep strain, agar, disc size, substance volume, time and temperature constant. Larger zone → more inhibition under these conditions. Different diffusion rates mean this does not prove effectiveness inside a patient. Zone area: Radius = diameter ÷ 2; area = πr². Diameter 12 mm → radius 6 mm → π × 6² = 113 mm² (3 s.f.). Use squared units. Subtract disc area only if asked. A clear zone means growth was inhibited. Repeated doubling: n = total time ÷ division time. Final population = start × 2ⁿ. 50 bacteria; 20-minute divisions; 2 h: 120 ÷ 20 = 6 doublings. 50 × 2⁶ = 3,200 = 3.2 × 10³. Keep time units consistent; apply the stated growth conditions.
